projects.title: Atlas
projects.nextAction: Move project out of OneDrive (e.g. C:\dev\atlas) so OneDrive stops reverting edits. Confirm Project Sheet renames + new layout look right after deploy.
projects.notes: Personal project management dashboard. Cloudflare Workers + D1 + Static Assets. Single worker (tb-atlas) serves both the API at /atlas/api/* and the static UI at /atlas/* on the toddboswell.com zone. Project list, log entries, and reflections all live in one D1 database (tb-atlas, id 19ef0420-72ea-4a51-986b-a749512ffc7e). The reflect and agent endpoints call the Claude API and need ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set as a Wrangler secret.
projects.dossier:
HOW IT WAS BUILT

Started from a deploy that wouldn't go out: D1 binding had an empty database_id placeholder. Three rounds of fixes, then UI polish.

1. D1 binding
   - Ran 'wrangler d1 list', got 19ef0420-72ea-4a51-986b-a749512ffc7e, plugged it into wrangler.toml.
   - Created schema.sql with projects, log_entries, reflections plus indexes. Applied with 'wrangler d1 execute tb-atlas --remote --file=./schema.sql'.

2. Static assets
   - Original wrangler.toml used the legacy [site] binding, but worker.js referenced env.ASSETS, which only exists with the new [assets] binding. So env.ASSETS was undefined, and serveStatic silently fell back to a placeholder string ('Atlas app - asset "/index.html"').
   - Switched to [assets] with explicit binding = "ASSETS". Removed the silent fallback so missing-binding errors surface as a 500 with a clear message.
   - Discovered that Cloudflare's static-assets binding maps asset paths to the worker's route pattern. With route www.toddboswell.com/atlas/* and assets at public/index.html, env.ASSETS.fetch() couldn't resolve them. The fetch fell through the zone and returned the apex toddboswell.com homepage HTML inside /atlas/ responses.
   - Fix: moved all assets to public/atlas/* so paths mirror the route. Simplified serveStatic to pass the request through to env.ASSETS without rewriting URLs (only special-case: /atlas and /atlas/ rewrite to /atlas/index.html).

3. Routing
   - Custom domain wasn't bound. Added [[routes]] in wrangler.toml: pattern www.toddboswell.com/atlas/*, zone_name toddboswell.com. Disabled workers.dev since only the custom domain is wanted.

4. UI polish (Project Sheet)
   - Renamed the modal from 'Character Sheet' to 'Project Sheet' (button label changed too).
   - Activity Log moved from the bottom of the main column into the right sidebar so it runs down the right side of the sheet.
   - Reflection (Ask Claude) moved to the bottom of the main column, with a top divider in accent color so it reads as the closing section.
   - Auto-save: any field change debounces an 800ms save for existing projects. New projects show 'new — click save to create'. Closing the modal (X, Escape, or backdrop click) saves first if there are unsaved changes.
   - Save indicator pill above Save/Delete: saved · saving… · unsaved changes · draft · save error.

5. Importer
   - Import flow now upserts by id: if the imported project's id matches one in state, it updates that project (PUT). Otherwise it creates a new one (POST). Accepts {projects:[...]}, a bare array, or a single project object.
   - This file (atlas-card.json) is meant to be re-imported to update the Atlas card itself.

OTHER FIXES
   - Removed two trailing-space bugs in the Anthropic API URL (https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages).
   - Wrapped listProjects/getProject in try/catch so missing tables return readable JSON errors, not Worker 1101 crashes.
   - Bumped the reflect/agent model from claude-3-haiku-20240307 to claude-haiku-4-5-20251001.

GOTCHAS LEARNED
   - OneDrive silently reverted file writes during this work. Several rounds of 'I edited the file' didn't stick because the project lives in C:\Users\fatba\onedrive\toddboswell.com\atlas. Move out of OneDrive next.
   - The 'Atlas app - asset' fallback string was misleading: it looked like an asset path, but it was a hardcoded stub that ran when env.ASSETS was undefined. Removing the fallback was a bigger fix than the asset path itself, because it stopped hiding the real cause.

projects.title: mimiboswell.com
projects.nextAction: Add mimiboswell.com + maboswell.com as custom domains in Netlify, point DNS at Netlify (DNS only, gray cloud), redeploy with updated _redirects, then delete the toddboswell.com Worker route for mimiboswell.com.
projects.notes: Mimi's domain. Two-domain setup: mimiboswell.com is canonical, maboswell.com redirects to it. Single Netlify site (mab-website) hosts a quiet M. placeholder at the root and her preserved recipe collection at /recipes/. Site is deployed and reachable at mab-website.netlify.app — DNS cutover still pending.
projects.dossier:
ARCHITECTURE
Single Netlify site (mab-website) serving both mimiboswell.com and maboswell.com. mimiboswell.com is canonical. maboswell.com 301-redirects to mimiboswell.com via _redirects rules at the deploy root. www variants of both also redirect to apex mimiboswell. Recipe site lives at mimiboswell.com/recipes/. Netlify free tier; Let's Encrypt auto-provisioned certs.

WHY NETLIFY
- Static hosting that accepts drag-and-drop deploys. No build step.
- Separate vendor from the toddboswell.com Cloudflare stack. Clean handoff if Mimi ever takes ownership.
- Friendlier dashboard than Cloudflare Pages for non-technical hand-off.
- Site can be transferred via account email change without touching code or DNS.

PLACEHOLDER DESIGN (root: /)
Fraunces serif on warm off-white #f5f3ee. Auto dark mode via prefers-color-scheme. Page reveal sequence ~2.6 seconds, all CSS, respects prefers-reduced-motion.

Reads top to bottom: M. monogram (clamp-sized big serif) → vertical rule → pilcrow ¶ (paragraph mark, in Fraunces at 2.75rem, 85% opacity) → MAB in small caps with 0.45em letter-spacing at 55% opacity. Grammar of that stack: name, pause, paragraph, signature. Quiet declaration without saying anything personal.

Mark history: started with asterism, then iterated to stet (proofreader's 'let it stand'), then settled on pilcrow as the final choice. Pilcrow is most universally readable as 'writing' while still being typographic rather than illustrative. Favicon is a path-drawn pilcrow shape (not text-based SVG, for Safari compatibility).

File is ~4KB single index.html. Hardened for Netlify with a netlify.toml (security headers, 5-min cache on HTML for fast updates) and _redirects.

RECIPE SITE (subdirectory: /recipes/)
Faithful preservation of Mimi's existing ehost recipe site. Kept the original Trebuchet MS / black-bordered / white-content look exactly. Same colors (#A35200 hover orange). Same structure (4 categories: Brunch / Sides / Mains / Sweets, plus index, plus 60 individual recipe pages).

Fixed under the hood:
- All 65 .shtml files renamed to .html, every internal link updated to match
- iso-8859-1 → UTF-8, all mangled '?' characters repaired (350? → 350°, don?t → don't, em-dashes restored)
- Broken HTML on side/maindish/sweets fixed (img tag missing closing >)
- Per-page titles generated from H3/H4 (was 'Mimi's Recipe Box' on every page)
- viewport meta tag added so it actually works on phones
- HTML5 doctype, modern <html lang='en'>
- Empty <style> blocks stripped
- chickensoup.html extension preserved (was already .html in original)

CSS rewrite preserves the original look but goes fluid:
- Removed absolute positioning that broke layout
- Same 760px max-width on desktop (preserves intent)
- Recipe pages: CSS grid, image left + text right on tablet+, stacked on phone
- Print stylesheet: nav hidden, single column, clean recipe printout

_redirects rules at deploy root:
1. /recipes/*.shtml → /recipes/:splat.html (301) — legacy ehost bookmarks still work
2. https://maboswell.com/* → https://mimiboswell.com/:splat (301!) — domain consolidation
3. https://www.maboswell.com/* → https://mimiboswell.com/:splat (301!)
4. https://www.mimiboswell.com/* → https://mimiboswell.com/:splat (301!) — apex canonical
5. /* → /index.html (200) — catch-all for placeholder

KEY DECISIONS
- Zero personal information on the placeholder. No name spelled out, no email, no bio, no photo, no social links.
- Title tag is just 'M.' to match the page register.
- robots noindex,nofollow on placeholder until she has real content.
- Recipe site lives at subfolder /recipes/, not its own subdomain. Single deploy, single cert.
- Both domains attached to one Netlify site rather than separate sites with proxy redirects. Simpler.
- mimiboswell.com chosen as canonical because it's the longer-standing/recognized domain. maboswell.com redirects to it.

DEPLOYMENT STATE (as of session)
- Site deployed to mab-website.netlify.app and rendering correctly
- Custom domains NOT YET added in Netlify
- DNS NOT YET pointed at Netlify
- Cloudflare Worker route for mimiboswell.com NOT YET deleted
- maboswell.com currently throws ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID — almost certainly Cloudflare orange-cloud proxying intercepting before Netlify can serve

DNS REQUIREMENTS (when you do the cutover)
For each of mimiboswell.com and maboswell.com in their Cloudflare zones:
- A record @ → 75.2.60.5 (Netlify IP, confirm with Netlify dashboard)
- CNAME www → mab-website.netlify.app
- BOTH records: DNS only (gray cloud), NOT proxied (orange cloud)
The gray cloud is critical. Netlify can't issue Let's Encrypt certs through Cloudflare's proxy.

FUTURE-YOU NOTES
- The whole placeholder is single index.html, ~4KB. Trivially portable to any static host.
- If Mimi wants to publish writing later: Ghost (~$9/mo, hosted, great writing UI) or Squarespace. Avoid building her something custom on Cloudflare Pages — that re-couples her to the toddboswell.com stack and defeats the portability goal.
- The pilcrow + MAB attribution can carry forward into whatever she builds next. Working visual identity, not just placeholder ornament.
- Recipe content is preservation-only. If she wants to expand, the existing template is hand-editable but the architecture (one .html file per recipe) doesn't scale gracefully past ~100 recipes. At that point migrate to a markdown + static-generator setup (Eleventy is a good fit for hand-off) or a hosted CMS.
- ehost.com (toddboswell.ehost.com/recipes/) is still serving the old version. Decide whether to keep paying for ehost or sunset that account. If sunsetting, set up an ehost-side redirect to mimiboswell.com/recipes/ first so Google doesn't lose the link equity.
